record.context_brief: Fundamental groups of elliptically connected manifolds
record.original_question: Let X be an elliptically connected complete Kähler manifold, meaning that any two points of X can be joined by a finite chain of holomorphic images of non-hyperbolic curves and complex tori. Must the fundamental group π1(X) be almost abelian? At least, must it be almost nilpotent?

evidence.quote:
CONJECTURE. If X is an elliptically connected complete K¨ahler manifold, then
the group π1(X) is almost abelian (or, in a weaker form, almost nilpotent).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a complete Kähler manifold $X$ elliptically connected if any two points of $X$ can be joined by a finite chain $C_1, C_2, \dots, C_k$ of irreducible compact complex curves, where each $C_i$ is the holomorphic image in $X$ of either a non-hyperbolic curve (i.e., $\mathbb{P}^1$ or an elliptic curve) or, more generally, of a complex torus (of arbitrary dimension), and consecutive curves $C_i, C_{i+1}$ share a common point.

Recall that a group $G$ is called almost abelian (respectively almost nilpotent) if it contains an abelian (respectively nilpotent) subgroup of finite index.

Question: Let $X$ be an elliptically connected complete Kähler manifold. Must its fundamental group $\pi_1(X)$ be almost abelian? If not, must $\pi_1(X)$ at least be almost nilpotent?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not locate a definitive resolution of this conjecture. Related results exist for rationally connected manifolds (where π₁ is finite) and for special Kähler manifolds (Campana's abelianity conjecture for fundamental groups of special compact Kähler manifolds, which is itself still largely open). No source was found that explicitly proves or disproves almost abelianity or almost nilpotency for π₁ of elliptically connected complete Kähler manifolds, so the status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: The fundamental group, rational connectedness and the positivity of Kähler manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Studies fundamental groups under rational/elliptic connectedness type hypotheses for Kähler manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Related connectedness/π₁ questions are still under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Solvable fundamental groups of algebraic varieties and Kähler manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Solvable linear or polycyclic π₁ of Kähler manifolds are virtually nilpotent.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist on virtual nilpotency under solvability assumptions, but not in the elliptically connected setting.

status_evidence.title: Notes on fundamental groups of Kähler manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Survey notes; no explicit resolution of the elliptic-connectedness conjecture is listed.
status_evidence.claim: No proof or counterexample of the conjecture is recorded in standard surveys.
